title: Whiteout Broadcast
status: concept-proposal (Creative Director, 2026-11-19; not approved; awaiting owner review)
hook_line: Snowed in. The radio started reading survival steps.
first_visual: An old kitchen radio glowing amber on a windowsill; outside, white nothing pressed to the glass.

beats.visual: Amber radio on the sill; whiteout pressed to the glass.
beats.vo: Snowed in. The radio started reading survival steps.

beats.visual: A soft tap on the glass; Ivy freezes.
beats.vo: 'Two: knocking on the roof is snow. Knocking on glass is not.'
'Three: close the curtains in Theo's room.' It knew his name.

beats.visual: Ivy reaches to turn the radio up; the plug dangles, the battery cover open and empty.
beats.vo: 'Four: turn me up.' It wasn't plugged in.

beats.visual: Key moment: a mouth-shaped melt in the frost moves with the words.
beats.vo: 'Five: come closer to the window. I can't hear you through the snow.'

beats.visual: Ivy switches the lamp off. Darkness. Radio silent.
Black; three soft knocks on glass.

ending: Ivy breaks step one and switches off the light. Silence. Then a knock on the glass.

originality_review: Original. A radio of survival steps from a non-radio source is our own construction. The ending avoids 'don't open the door': the threat is at the glass, and she chooses darkness.
scores_basis: Initial editorial judgement, 2026-11-19. topic_demand is an estimate linked to research/WEEKLY_TREND_REPORT.md categories, not a measurement of this concept.
concept: Snowed in, Ivy hears an amber radio read calm survival steps that grow more personal, ending with 'come to the window'. The radio is unplugged. The voice comes from the frost on the glass.

hooks.line: Snowed in. The radio started reading survival steps.
hooks.first_visual: An old kitchen radio glowing amber on a windowsill; outside, white nothing pressed to the glass.

hooks.line: Step three used my nephew's name.
hooks.first_visual: A radio dial glowing; a woman turning toward a child's door.
A dangling plug, an empty battery compartment.

hooks.line: Knocking on the roof is snow. Knocking on the glass is not.
hooks.first_visual: A frosted kitchen window, a soft tap.

hooks.line: Step five: come closer to the window.
hooks.first_visual: A mouth-shaped melt forming in frost.

setting: Ivy's kitchen during a whiteout; Winter Lane invisible beyond the glass.
conflict: Ivy wants to follow official-sounding advice to stay safe.
escalation: Light, knock rules, then Theo's name, then 'turn me up', then the unplugged cord.
reveal: A mouth-shaped melt in the frost moves with the words.
